a human adenovirus-based vaccine reprograms immune response and reverses chronic chagasic heart disease.

vaccination with replication-defective adenovirus carrying T. cruzi antigen genes induced a specific immune response, reduced heart parasitism, electrical abnormalities and tissue damage, and improved survival in a mouse model of chronic Chagas disease.

the development of a vaccine for Chagas disease, which is a prototypical tropical neglected disease.
the development of a vaccine for the prevention and treatment of Chagas disease.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a human adenovirus-based vaccine can be used to re-program immune response and reverse cardiac tissue damage in Chagas disease.

the vaccine-based immunostimulation by rAdVax might offer a rational and alternative strategy for re-programming of the immune response to prevent and, moreover, reverse tissue injury in Chagasic cardiomyopaty.
rAdVax is a promising therapeutic vaccine for the treatment of Chagas’ cardiomyopathy, which could be applied in patients at different stages of the disease, including those with advanced CCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a vaccine based on recombinant adenoviurses can be a good alternative to stimulate a protective immune response in order to prevent or reverse chronic chagasic cardomyopathy.
a vaccine based on recombinant adenocarcinoma viruses (rAds), carrying T. cruzi sequences, is capable to induce specific immunity and reverse chronic chagasic heart injury.
a human type 5 adenovirus-based Trypanosoma Cruzii therapeutic vaccine re-programs immune response and reverses chronic cardiomyopathy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

vaccination is a potential strategy for reprogramming the immune response in Chagas’ disease, and that the use of a vaccine based on human adenoviruses could be a promising strategy for reprogramming immune response in Chagasic patients, and for the recovery of tissue damage in Chagas’ cardiomyopathy.
vaccination with rAdVAX, a human Type 5 Ad-based vaccine, can reverse the chronic chagasic heart disease, which is the main clinical manifestation of Chagas disease.

the use of rAdVax as a therapeutic vaccine in a murine model of CD can re-program immune responses and reduce cardiac tissue damage in the chronic phase, suggesting that it could be used as a therapeutic vaccine for CD patients.
